title: How soon after inversion does the Fed cut?

groups.afterHike: Last target move was a hike

methods.instrument: Treasury constant-maturity yields in percent, quoted on an investment basis. Long yield minus short yield, in basis points. Thresholds compare the spread, not a probability or futures price.
methods.signal: Main signal: today's spread is at or below −12.5 bp and the previous common trading day's spread was above −12.5 bp. Quotes are published to 1 bp precision. A strict negative spread and a threshold of −25 bp are separate sensitivities.
methods.episode: Accept a fresh crossing only if at least 12 calendar months have elapsed since the last accepted crossing in that curve. Do not re-enter an existing inversion at its anniversary. The rate panel begins in December 1998 to initialize the rule before 2000. Follow-up windows do not overlap within each primary curve.
methods.outcome: A hit is the first subsequent announced cut to the FOMC target (upper bound from 16 December 2008) strictly after signal close and no later than its six- or twelve-calendar-month anniversary. This includes further cuts in an easing cycle. When 'last move was a hike' is selected, a hit is the first cut after a hiking phase.
methods.timing: All target changes from 2000 match exactly one San Francisco Fed statement on the ALFRED target-change date or the preceding calendar day. Use the announcement date, including intermeeting and Sunday decisions. The 16 December 2008 transition from 1% to 0–0.25% counts once. Asset purchases and guidance alone do not count.
methods.denominator: Both signals and comparison trading days require complete follow-up through the last common date. Later observations are excluded at that horizon even if a cut is already observable. Null denotes incomplete follow-up or an empty group. All dates use the latest available common observation across four maturities; no interpolation or forward-filled yields.
methods.benchmark: The unconditional base is the share of all eligible trading dates followed by a cut at the same horizon, subject to the same subgroup and maturity requirement. The year-matched base gives the eligible trading-day mean within each signal's entry year, then averages those means over signals. It guards against concentration in years with many cuts; it is a retrospective comparator.
methods.regimes: Pre-2008 = 2000–2007; calendar 2008 is separate; post-2008 starts in 2009. Assignment uses signal date. The acute-crisis sensitivity removes signal-to-horizon intervals touching 15 September through 16 December 2008, inclusive. The above-floor group requires the target upper bound above 0.25% on entry.
methods.uncertainty: Few distinct easing cycles. Primary signal windows are non-overlapping within each curve, but the two curves may share an event and base-day outcomes overlap. Percentages are descriptive sample frequencies. Treat all crossings and all inverted trading days as dependent sensitivity counts, not extra independent experiments.
methods.chart: Monthly chart points are the last common observation in each month; the latest month may be partial. Signals and hits are computed from daily observations.
methods.scope: The first subsequent cut can follow intervening hikes. Treasury slopes also reflect term premia, issuance, liquidity and risk expectations. No excess returns, transaction costs or causal effects are estimated.
